A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeRAF, with matching authors, core architecture, datasets, and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v3's added Appendices K–O.

before.justification: v2 reports original acoustic synthesis, visual rendering, few-shot, and ablation results on SoundSpaces, RAF, and RWAVS, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments on multi-scene training, unseen sources, furniture proximity, and separate modality training.

M1.justification: v3 adds a staged multi-scene training variant: first fit one NeRF per scene, then train a shared ResNet3D and acoustic field using scene grids and mixed-scene batches (Section 4.2). This changes the training procedure while retaining the original architecture, losses, and joint-training mode.

E1.justification: SoundSpaces, RAF, and RWAVS coverage is retained. Appendix M adds evaluation at source poses entirely unseen during training, extending RAF's previous scenario of unseen source-microphone pairs with overlapping sources. Multi-scene experiments reuse existing SoundSpaces rooms.

E2.justification: Appendix N and Table A5 introduce a sequentially trained NeRF-then-NAcF comparator against joint NeRAF. This is a limited addition of an internal comparison method; comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables and few-shot comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained. Added experiments introduce an 85%/15% source-level RAF split, mixed-scene training without increasing model size, and a fully pretrained NeRF for the separate-training control. Figure A2 also adds a 25%-training-data condition on RAF.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained grid, loss, and few-shot analyses, v3 substantially expands diagnostic evaluation: furniture-proximity effects, unseen-source generalization, whether joint training benefits each modality, and whether one acoustic model can learn multiple scenes (Appendices L–O and Table 3). These address previously untested applicability and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are conducted six times and results averaged. v3 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, variability reporting, or significance-testing procedure; the added results retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results cover multi-scene learning, furniture proximity, unseen sources, and separate training. For example, new Table 3 reports mean T60 of 2.29% for single-scene versus 2.24% for multi-scene training. Figures 7 and A2 revise existing plotted values, and A2 adds 25%-data results. The no-grid EDT entry changes without explanation from 0.0212 to 0.212 (v2 Table 3; v3 Table 4). Main benchmark Tables 1, 2, A2, and A3 retain their values.

T1.justification: The field definitions, rendering equations, losses, and metric formulas retain their mathematical substance. v3 removes an empty equation-numbering line and reorders equivalent RAF inputs in Appendix A. Appendix K adds physical motivation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about 3D-conditioned acoustic fields, improved RIR synthesis and data efficiency, sparse-view rendering benefits, and independent modalities without co-located sensors. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 narrows the per-scene training limitation to NeRF. Section 4.2 acknowledges that staged multi-scene training forfeits visual cross-modal benefits. Appendix N attributes comparable joint/separate audio performance to both retaining 3D grid conditioning, while Appendix K expands the physical rationale for those priors.

D1.justification: The new multi-scene recipe documents pretrained per-scene NeRFs, 128-resolution grids, batches drawn across scenes, and 1,024 grid features per scene (Section 4.2 and Appendix O). Existing optimizer, hardware, training-budget, and code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work positioning retain the same works. Appendix K elaborates the existing argument for 3D scene conditioning over camera-local information in Liang et al. (2023a;b), without introducing a new prior-work relationship or novelty claim.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. v3 inserts a multi-scene subsection and Appendices K–O, adds a short Nerfstudio explanation and Appendix A pointer, and makes limited edits to limitations, affiliation, contact information, and notation.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 3 and Tables A4–A6, relocates retained Tables 1–2 and Figure 7, and redraws the few-shot plots with changed axes and legends. The original ablation table becomes Table 4. Most illustrations and the overall visual design remain recognizable, with minor spacing and header-rule changes.

improvement.justification: The unseen-source and separate-training tests improve evidence about positional generalization and the role of joint learning. Multi-scene results also support a more precise scene-dependence limitation. These additions strengthen an otherwise stable paper. The unexplained tenfold no-grid EDT revision introduces a localized numerical reliability concern, but the added controls and clearer applicability boundaries provide a modest net benefit.
